title: rbac v2: enforce KMS region pinning + audit logging enhancements
author: Avery Kim
description:
Motivation: Customers in regulated regions require strict enforcement of KMS key residency and full audit trails tying RBAC decisions to KMS key metadata and regions. RBAC v1 allowed advisory checks in some paths; this PR upgrades RBAC v2 to enforce KMS region pinning and extends audit events to include KMS key id, region, and policy decision context.

What this PR does: 1) Adds an enforcement layer that validates KMS key region against the resource's allowed residency constraints during the RBAC decision path; decision failures return clear authorization errors (HTTP 403) with auditable reason codes. 2) Enhances audit payloads to include kms_key_id, kms_region, and enforcement_reason fields. 3) Adds DB migration to backfill existing RBAC policy metadata and a migration script to tag policies with residency constraints where omitted. 4) Introduces feature flag rbac_v2_kms_enforcement (off by default) to allow staged rollout + canary enabling per-tenant. 5) Updates docs and operator Helm values for Redwood Private to expose KMS residency config.

Design notes: - Enforcement is implemented in rbac/v2/enforcer so all decision points (serve path, admin APIs, private installer flows) pass through the unified enforcer. The enforcer consults policy.attachments.kms_residency and compares against the kms key region reported by the KMS client. - KMS client now surfaces region in its KeyMetadata response; a short TTL cache avoids extra RPCs under high QPS. - Audit events are versioned (audit.v2) so downstream sinks can migrate without loss of prior schema. - Rollout strategy: start with feature flag off, enable in staging and a subset of tenants, monitor audit drift and auth failures, then flip to on by default after two weeks of stable signals.

Testing: unit tests for policy matching and KMS metadata parsing; integration tests exercising RBAC failures when region mismatch occurs; e2e against redwood-private with mock KMS and a small canary tenant. Load tests verify cache reduces extra KMS calls. Security scan and SAST run green after minor fixes.

Risk & mitigations: - Risk: accidental denial of service for tenants without policy metadata. Mitigation: default-to-allow when policy residency unset while feature flag is off; migration script tags obvious policies and operators can opt-in per-tenant. - Risk: increased latency from KMS calls. Mitigation: local TTL cache + background refresh; metrics added (rbac.kms_cache.hit/miss, rbac.enforce.latency).

Migration steps for operators (short): 1) Run the included SQL migration to add residency column to rbac_policies. 2) Run `scripts/backfill_kms_residency.sh` to infer residency from existing configs. 3) Toggle feature flag for a small set of tenants and monitor `rbac.enforce.denials` and `audit.events.kms`. 4) Gradually expand and flip default.

References: Linear ENG-7023, SEC-329, support ticket SUP-1182. Related PRs: prior RBAC V2 policy shape changes in pr-53210.
